svg.title: Smart-home radio paths across 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, 6 GHz, and Thread border routers
svg.desc: Diagram showing a single-SSID multi-band router serving 2.4 GHz smart plugs and sensors on channels 1, 6, and 11, 5 GHz and 6 GHz high-bandwidth devices, and Thread 802.15.4 low-power devices via a Thread Border Router.
svg.text: One Network Name (SSID), Multiple Smart-Home Radio Paths
How Apple, Google Nest Wifi, and Matter/Thread separate high-speed clients from low-power devices
PRIMARY ROUTER
Single Primary SSID
• 2.4 GHz + 5 GHz (+ 6 GHz)
• WPA2 / WPA3 Transition
• mDNS / Local LAN discovery
• Client isolation OFF on
Matter commissioning LAN
Apple #102766 Recommended
PATH 1 · 2.4 GHz WI-FI (CHANNELS 1, 6, 11 · 20 MHz WIDTH)
Longest Wall Range · Lowest Bandwidth · Most Embedded IoT Chips
Smart plugs, garage controllers, leak valves, thermostats, 2.4 GHz cameras
PATH 2 · 5 GHz & 6 GHz WI-FI (40 / 80 / 160 MHz CHANNELS)
High Throughput · Lower Congestion · Shorter Wall Penetration
Phones, laptops, Apple TV / streaming boxes, dual-band doorbells, mesh backhaul
PATH 3 · THREAD MESH (IEEE 802.15.4) VIA THREAD BORDER ROUTER
Low-Power IPv6 Mesh · Does Not Use Wi-Fi Credentials Directly
Battery locks, contact sensors, Matter-over-Thread switches bridged to home LAN
Setup Tip: Keep phone and device on the same LAN/VLAN during onboarding; test signal at the final mounting spot before drilling.
